newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar backs off, NY weakness sets pace.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar backs off, NY weakness sets pace.

text.p: White sugar futures struggled to hold above earlier lows but bearish sentiment spilling over from a weak New York market continued to pressure values, traders said on Tuesday.

At 1730 GMT May was down $2.10 at $306.00, just above its intraday low of $305.50. Traders noted interest in the May/August switch, which persistently fluctuated between positive and negative territory.
August was down $1.90 at $305.50 and volume reached a solid 1,725 lots, mostly in the two front positions but boosted by crossed trades on the spot position.

The London board's mixed structure calmed during afternoon trading but most attention was centred on the fortunes of the spot March raws contract and the May/May white premium, which continued to hover around $66.
Technical analysts pegged May whites support at just above $303.00 -- an upward trendline dating from last month's trough of $293.50.

European traders said they were still awaiting the results of Iraq's tender to buy 120,000 tonnes of sugar under the U.N. oil-for-food deal but noted that details were likely to be sketchy for some time.
The Paris market followed a similar trading pattern to London and all values lost ground.
May was down $2.30 at $305.50 and August down $2.00 at $305.30. Matif volume totalled 746 lots.
